title: Runbook Execlet Hub — lightweight admin execution and idempotency layer
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Build a compact ‘Execlet Hub’ that converts canonical runbook steps into idempotent, observable tasklets that can be executed by first-line support tools and the admin CLI. The hub must: 1) provide a minimal runtime for step execution (safety-checked, permission-gated), 2) expose a declarative runbook-to-task DSL for designers/PMs, and 3) surface per-step telemetry (latency, success/failure, side-effect diffs) to the Console.

Why: Current runbooks live as docs or long-form scripts. Teams repeatedly reimplement similar small admin fixes with subtle differences and risk. Packaging steps as typed, idempotent tasks reduces blast radius, enables dry-run, autosuggestion in support UIs, and unlocks automated remediation pipelines while preserving human oversight.

Non-goals: This project does not replace long-running coordinated playbooks (multi-step human workflows) nor does it ship a new policy engine — it focuses on unit-runbook steps and the exec runtime surface.

Key design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Idempotency model: choose optimistic idempotency keys + compensating checks vs strict transactional undo records. We selected optimistic idempotency (checksums + guarded retries) to keep runtime small and interoperable with existing services.
- Permissions model: leverage existing RBAC tokens from the admin console and add a scoped exec token concept for short-lived tasklets. This avoids a big permission redesign.
- Execution model: sandboxed python/golet vs in-process node workers. We decided on a lightweight containerized execlet (OCI micro-container) pattern for security and language flexibility; initial runtime uses a pared-down Go shim image.

Acceptance criteria:
- Conversion tooling: CLI command that converts at least 8 canonical runbook snippets into tasklets with typed inputs and dry-run capability.
- Runtime: Execlet service that executes tasklets with a per-step timeout and returns structured result (status, diff, logs) to caller.
- Observability: Each execution emits traces, error codes, and token-level cost/time to the Console. Dashboards for execlet success rate and mean time-to-execute created.
- Safety: Permission gating and audit logs appear in Customer Audit stream; any execlet performing destructive actions must require an explicit approval flag.

Migration/rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only — wire a small set of low-risk runbooks (user-reset, log-rotate, snapshot-backup) behind a feature flag.
2) Beta: add CLI/Console surface for suggestions and dry-run; auto-suggest runlets in support playbooks.
3) GA: expose to Dedicated and Private deployments with hardened exec images and KMS-integrated secrets.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: execlets could be used to escalate privileges — mitigation: short-lived scoped tokens, RBAC audit, and mandatory approval for dangerous ops.
- Risk: state divergence after partial runs — mitigation: idempotency checks and compensating step templates + explicit undo snippets stored alongside runlets.

Telemetry and metrics to collect:
- per-step success/failure, error taxonomy, mean execution time, dry-run vs live-run ratio, top failing runlets, and operator actions following failures.

Next technical tasks (high-level):
- Implement runbook-to-tasklet CLI converter (prototype v0.1) — owner: Riley
- Build execlet Go shim and container image registry pipeline — owner: Backend infra
- Hook trace/metrics into Console observability backend and add minimal dashboard — owner: Observability team
- Draft operator-facing UX copy and dry-run flow in Console — owner: PM (linked)

Linking artifacts: see attachments field for design doc and initial PRs.

- Execlet service returns structured step result and emits telemetry
- Console dashboard shows execlet health and per-tasklet metrics
- RBAC gating and audit logs for all live executions
